concept: Snackbar is Toast's strip of matte plastic placed once, centred just above the phone's bottom nav, saying what just happened with a printed glyph and word and offering one key that undoes it.
family_difference: Toast stacks up to three notes at the inline end with a close key each; Snackbar shows one message at a time centred above the bottom nav, has no close key, carries at most one action key that undoes, replaces itself when a new one is posted, and stays a polite status even when something failed.

default_to_avoid.pattern: Material dark snackbar, a near-black bar with white text and a coloured action word
default_to_avoid.why_not: A dark bar on a light screen is a second material and a coloured action word is a link in an accent hue; P1 and P5 keep one plastic and ink at full step.

default_to_avoid.pattern: snackbar that slides in from the edge and bounces before it settles
default_to_avoid.why_not: P6 allows motion only on a change of state, and a bounce is choreography that pulls the eye away from the room.

references.source: Braun SK 61 radio-phonograph (Dieter Rams, 1962): the one changing reading sits in a fixed slot under the controls
WCAG 2.2 success criterion 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable: a message that leaves on its own can be paused
WAI-ARIA status role: a polite live region read without moving focus

derivation.consequence: sits where the hand expects it (lower or right of the display)
derivation.form: The strip sits centred just above the bottom nav, so Undo is under the thumb that just removed the lamp.

derivation.consequence: links, borders, icons, selections and charts never use it
derivation.form: The Undo key is a plastic key, never orange, and the tone is a printed glyph with its word beside it.

derivation.consequence: fixed positions, so a unit's layout does not reflow between states
derivation.form: The strip floats over the page and never pushes the nav or the content; one message shows at a time.

options.name: strip over the nav, Toast's plastic strip centred just above the bottom nav with one Undo key
printed on the nav, the bottom nav grows a row and prints the message in it
counter window, the message in an LCD window strip with the key beside it

variants.reason: A keeps Toast's one plastic and puts Undo under the thumb without moving anything (P1, P6); B changes the nav's height while it shows, which moves every section word, and C adds a second display window that competes with the device's own (P2).

root.why: The strip is matte plastic at float height with a lit top-left hairline, the same body as Toast.

head.why: The glyph and the status word sit together at the start of the line, printed on the strip.

glyph.why: The tone glyph is printed with the two pixel stroke, flat on the plastic, never filled.

status.why: The status word is set at the label size in medium weight so the tone is read as a word.

message.why: The message is set at body size in the primary ink, short and in the past tense.

key.why: The one action key sits at the inline end of the strip, where the thumb reaches it.

neutral.why: A plain note prints its glyph in the info ink, the word beside it in the primary ink.

positive.why: A done message prints its tick in the positive ink, never as a tinted strip.

warning.why: A warning prints its triangle in the primary ink, so shape and word carry it alone.

critical.why: A failure prints its octagon in the critical ink beside the word Failed, never orange.

region.why: The region is fixed and centred at the bottom of the screen, so the message always appears in one place.

aboveNav.why: On a phone the region lifts by the nav's height so the strip sits just above the printed sections.

data-state=open.why: The strip rises a few pixels and fades in on the enter easing, and leaves faster on the exit easing.

@media orientation: landscape.why: On a wide screen the nav is a rail at the side, so the strip drops to the bottom edge inset.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under reduced motion the strip appears and leaves at once, with no rise and no fade.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the strip keeps a real border and the glyph takes the text colour so both survive.

opacity.why: The strip fades with its short rise so it arrives and leaves as one change of state.

transform.why: The only travel is motion.rise, a few pixels upward, over motion.enter in and motion.exit out.
